Run eSVD-DE on a Seurat object, with cohort filtering and gene status

Source: R/eSVD_helper.R
eSVD_helper.Rd

The recommended entry point. It wraps eSVD in the five steps a real dataset needs and eSVD itself refuses to perform:

  1. Drop individuals with fewer than min_cells_per_id cells, with a warning naming them (filter_cohort).

  2. Check min_cells, min_ids, min_ids_per_arm and min_cells_casecontrol on the filtered cohort; on failure, warn and return NA (filter_cohort).

  3. Label every gene's gene_status from the filtered counts and remove the genes whose counts are all zero. This runs after the drop, because a gene expressed only in a dropped individual becomes all-zero.

  4. Call eSVD on what remains; every further argument goes through ....

  5. Reinsert the removed genes at their original positions.

Usage

eSVD_helper(
  batch_var_prefix,
  case_control_levels,
  case_control_var,
  categorical_vars,
  id_var,
  numerical_vars,
  seurat_obj,
  min_cells = 20,
  min_cells_casecontrol = 20,
  min_cells_per_id = 3,
  min_ids = 4,
  min_ids_per_arm = 2,
  verbose = 0,
  ...
)

Arguments

batch_var_prefix

NULL, or a regular expression matched against the names of categorical_vars; the matching covariates are treated as batch variables and their coefficients are not reparameterized.

case_control_levels

Character vector of length 2 giving the two levels of case_control_var, control first, then case. Reversing them flips the sign of every test statistic.

case_control_var

Name of the column in seurat_obj@meta.data holding the case-control status.

categorical_vars

Character vector of column names in seurat_obj@meta.data to adjust for as factors (one-hot encoded, first level dropped), or NULL. A variable with a single level is dropped.

id_var

Name of the column in seurat_obj@meta.data naming each cell's individual (donor).

numerical_vars

Character vector of column names in seurat_obj@meta.data to adjust for as numerical covariates, or NULL. They are rescaled by format_covariates.

seurat_obj

A Seurat object whose "RNA" assay has a "counts" layer (genes by cells) and whose meta.data holds the variables above.

min_cells

Reject a cohort with this many cells or fewer, after the drop.

min_cells_casecontrol

Reject a cohort in which either arm has this many cells or fewer.

min_cells_per_id

Drop every individual with fewer than this many cells; 0 or at least 3.

min_ids

Reject a cohort with this many individuals or fewer, pooled across arms.

min_ids_per_arm

Reject a cohort in which either arm has fewer than this many individuals. The default 2 is the smallest number for which the Welch degrees of freedom are defined.

verbose

Integer; 0 is silent.

...

Further arguments to eSVD, such as k, bool_diet, cap_multiplier or intermediate_save.

Value

Either NA (the cohort was rejected; see the warning), or the eSVD object returned by eSVD with the removed genes reinserted as described above and an added element gene_status.

Details

gene_status is a named factor over the original genes, in their original order, with levels "analyzed" (1) and "all_zero" (2). An all_zero gene comes back with NA in every per-gene estimate (teststat_vec, case_mean, control_mean, case_var, control_var, log2fc_vec, log2fc_se_vec, pvalue_list$df_vec, pvalue_list$gaussian_teststat, and the rows of y_mat, z_mat, nuisance_vec and the other per-gene vectors of estimate_nuisance in the final fit), a pvalue_list$log10pvalue of 0 (that is, a p-value of 1) and a pvalue_list$fdr_vec of 1. The empirical null and the Benjamini-Hochberg adjustment are computed on the analyzed genes only, which is guaranteed by construction: eSVD never sees an all-zero gene.

Removing all-zero genes changes the factorization of the retained genes, because an all-zero column is not a zero column of the residual matrix the initialization decomposes. Results for the retained genes therefore differ from a run that kept the all-zero genes; they equal a run of eSVD on the filtered object exactly.

Examples

# \donttest{
if(requireNamespace("SeuratObject", quietly = TRUE)){
  set.seed(10)
  sim <- generate_null(cell_per_person = 15, num_genes = 40,
                       num_individuals = 8)
  meta_df <- data.frame(sim$covariates[, c("CC", "Sex", "Age")])
  meta_df$Sex <- factor(meta_df$Sex)
  meta_df$Individual <- sim$metadata_individual
  rownames(meta_df) <- rownames(sim$obs_mat)
  # Seurat rewrites "gene_1" as "gene-1" (with a warning); rename first
  count_mat <- Matrix::t(sim$obs_mat)
  rownames(count_mat) <- gsub("_", "", rownames(count_mat))
  seurat_obj <- SeuratObject::CreateSeuratObject(counts = count_mat,
                                                 meta.data = meta_df)

  esvd_obj <- eSVD_helper(batch_var_prefix = NULL,
                          case_control_levels = c("0", "1"),
                          case_control_var = "CC",
                          categorical_vars = "Sex",
                          id_var = "Individual",
                          numerical_vars = "Age",
                          seurat_obj = seurat_obj,
                          k = 2,
                          max_iter = 5)
  table(esvd_obj$gene_status)
  utils::head(report_results(esvd_obj))
}
